# Synthetic landslide sensor dataset

**THIS IS SYNTHETIC DATA.** It was generated by `generate_dataset.py` (seed 42) from simple mathematical models and random numbers.
It is **not** actual sensor measurements and the risk labels are **not** validated landslide predictions.
Thresholds and rules are illustrative assumptions. Do not report results on this data as real-world accuracy.

Rows: 14400 (6 nodes x 2400 samples, one sample every 5 minutes, starting 2025-06-01 00:00:00, sorted by node then time).

## Columns
| Column | Unit / values | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| row_id | integer | row number |
| timestamp | datetime | sample time (synthetic calendar) |
| node_id | N01-N06 | sensor node |
| gyro_x_dps, gyro_y_dps, gyro_z_dps | degrees per second | angular velocity of the node (ground tilt/creep) |
| rainfall_intensity_mm_h | mm per hour | rain rate |
| rainfall_accum_24h_mm | mm | rain total over the previous 24 h |
| humidity_rh_pct | % relative humidity | air humidity |
| temperature_c | degrees Celsius | air temperature |
| vibration_g | g (RMS magnitude) | vibration magnitude |
| environmental_scenario | text | Normal, Increasing Rainfall, Heavy Rainfall, Ground Movement, Elevated Vibration, or combinations joined with " + " |
| landslide_risk_label | Normal / Elevated Risk / High Risk | illustrative rule on the TRUE environment (below) |
| sensor_fault_label | Normal / Offset / Gain / Stuck-at / Out-of-bound / Missing | fault injected into the reading |
| faulty_sensor | gyroscope / rainfall / humidity / temperature / vibration / no_fault | which sensor is faulty |
| fault_episode_id | integer (0 = none) | id of the fault window; use it to split train/test by episode |
| dataset_source | text | marks the data as synthetic |

## Assumptions
* Rain: 7 regional storms (light, moderate, heavy) shared by all nodes with per-node scale (0.85-1.15) and noise.
* Temperature: daily cycle (warmest ~15:00) + slow weather drift + rain cooling. Humidity falls as temperature rises and rises in rain (capped at 100).
* Ground movement: smooth, slowly changing-direction angular velocity (peak 0.35-2.8 deg/s); heavy storms can trigger a movement zone on one node and its neighbours.
* Vibration: small baseline plus bursty episodes (peak 0.06-0.25 g), sometimes during movement.
* Environment flags (from TRUE values): Heavy Rainfall if rain >= 15.0 mm/h; Increasing Rainfall while rain is rising (>= 1 mm/h, not heavy); Ground Movement if |angular velocity| >= 0.2 deg/s; Elevated Vibration if vibration >= 0.04 g.
* Risk rule (illustrative): points per TRUE value - rain intensity >= 20.0/40.0 mm/h, 24 h rain >= 150.0/250.0 mm, angular speed >= 0.3/1.0 deg/s, vibration >= 0.05/0.15 g (1 point / 2 points). Score 2-3 = Elevated Risk, >= 4 = High Risk, held for 6 samples.
* Labels for scenario and risk come from the TRUE environment, so a sensor fault never changes them.

## Sensor faults
One sensor per fault window; windows on a node never overlap (10 windows per node, all five types).
* Offset: constant bias added (stays inside the sensor range).
* Gain: reading multiplied by a wrong factor (0.4-0.7 or 1.5-2.5, stays inside range).
* Stuck-at: reading frozen at the value when the fault began.
* Out-of-bound: values outside the sensor's range (and physically impossible).
* Missing: the sensor's columns are empty (NaN). **This is the only place where missing values occur, and it is intentional.**
* A fault window is accepted only if it changes the reading by a clearly visible amount, so no fault is invisible.
* Faults start and stop abruptly and affect one sensor only, whereas real environmental changes are smooth and show up on several sensors and neighbouring nodes. This is how faults are kept distinguishable from genuine changes.

## Rows per fault type and sensor in this run (computed by the script)
| Fault \ sensor | gyroscope | humidity | rainfall | temperature | vibration |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Gain | 0 | 293 | 129 | 151 | 90 |
| Missing | 150 | 122 | 57 | 43 | 138 |
| Offset | 164 | 22 | 0 | 205 | 226 |
| Out-of-bound | 48 | 51 | 159 | 85 | 143 |
| Stuck-at | 0 | 158 | 401 | 217 | 0 |

Gain and Stuck-at faults are only generated where they would be clearly visible; for a sensor whose signal is almost flat for most of the time (gyroscope, vibration) some combinations may therefore have zero rows.

## Limitations
Synthetic physics is simplified (no terrain, soil type, real rainfall-triggering thresholds or real sensor drift). Models trained on this data only show that a pipeline works; they say nothing about real landslide prediction.
`..._clean_reference.csv` holds the same rows without faults, for checking only - do not use it as ML input.
